problem:
Consider the set ${{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t),{p}_{3}(t)}$ of polynomials from $R[t],$ where

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=1+t+2{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=-2+3t+{t}^{2},\,{p}_{3}(t)=3t+3{t}^{2}.
$$

 

If the set is linearly dependent, find the value of $\frac{{x}_{3}}{{x}_{2}}$ from a non-zero solution of ${x}_{1}\cdot {p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}\cdot {p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}\cdot {p}_{3}(t)=0.$
worked_solution:
If the set is linearly dependent, then there exist ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ not all zero such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}{p}_{3}(t)=0.
$$

Otherwise, if ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0,$ the set is linearly independent.

Substituting the given expressions for ${p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t),$ and ${p}_{3}(t)$ into the above equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(1+t+2{t}^{2})+{x}_{2}(-2+3t+{t}^{2})+{x}_{3}(3t+3{t}^{2}) & =0 \\ ({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2})+({x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3})t+(2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}){t}^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The final equation is true for every $t$ if and only if 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we consider the corresponding augmented matrix and reduce it to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd. Hence, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable.

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-\frac{3}{5}{x}_{3}.$ Substitute it into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}-2(-\frac{3}{5}{x}_{3})=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-\frac{6}{5}{x}_{3}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{6}{5}{x}_{3} \\ -\frac{3}{5}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Finally, for any ${x}_{3}\ne 0,$ we obtain 

$$
\frac{{x}_{3}}{{x}_{2}}=\frac{{x}_{3}}{(-\frac{3}{5}{x}_{3})}=-\frac{5}{3}.
$$
